description: Screen the companies StockLens scores nightly by region, exchange, sector, industry, market-cap band and trading volume, sorted by one of the six StockLens scores or by market cap, volume or ticker, and return the top or bottom N. Every list is computed inside one listing market: the one named in macro_in or exchange_in, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result name it, so always say which market the rows are from, and when the person named no market, that others are covered, without screening them. For another market the person asks for (US, CA, EU, CH, GB, JP), call again naming it; never merge or compare lists across markets. multiple_markets and market_not_covered mean nothing was ranked: relay message. There is no popularity ordering; ask the person to choose another. Use it for any top, best, worst or filtered list, never one built from get_market_summary or general knowledge. To compare only companies the person names, call get_shortlist_summary instead. It has no valuation, price-target or growth filter; say so rather than calling a score sort one. status ranked means the requested order was used. When a ranked result carries message, relay it; it states what the ranking covers, so never present the rows as a ranking of more than that. browse_substituted means a score order was asked for and market-cap order with scores hidden was returned, so never describe those rows as ranked by score. locked means no companies are named; relay message verbatim. access_tier and reach_capped_at say what the caller can sort and how far; signed_in_as names their account. Report every returned row in its actual order and retain the population and access/substitution message. Where reading_ref and inspection are supplied, inspect only the company the person asks about; never fetch every row. When findings is present, explain findings.leading, then findings.first_answer, instead of key_drivers, as findings.claim allows: strongest, they moved this score most; strongest_first, the first moved it most and the second is another factor; explained, describe what the available evidence shows, with no biggest-mover sentence. Give a finding's fact figure with its own period, which can differ from the reading's date and from another finding's. A next look is findings.next_looks[0], or the second when the first's topic was already covered for this company in the conversation or misses the person's ask; skip both when both were covered, and never mention the one you do not ask. When the person asks directly for a figure a next look carries, give it with its period, then end with the other next look's question if it is still new. Otherwise ask that one question, in its words or your own, as the answer's final line, after any link. Never state, round or hint at any figure from next_looks before the person says yes. On a yes, give only its answer as given (the company figure with its period, and for a comparison the peer figure, statistic and group), without another call and without computing anything from the figures, then stop: no other offer, menu, save or analysis. After that answer, end with the other next look's question if it is still new; otherwise stop. A finding's qualification speaks only of that trailing P/E reading: when applied is true, say in the same sentence that the company's qualifying_measure of company_figure (trailing period to period_end) eased how StockLens weighed its P/E of pe_figure against peer_median for peer_group (a blended peer mark when peer_basis is blended, never a median of companies), and how it still reads there (remaining_assessment); when applied is false, mention the figure only as context, never as easing anything, whatever the finding's own label says. When qualifying_ref names another finding in the answer, it is the same figure: say it once, keeping both findings. Never present it as a change to the overall score or a view of the stock as a whole. For a finding tied to a source, give its event_date with the event (On the Oct 29 earnings call, In its Nov 8 filing; add the year across a year boundary). An insider transaction uses its trade date. For measured activity name the event_window_start and event_window_end, never a single latest article, filing or trade. Only the current result's dated reasons and questions qualify. Never substitute the reading's date or bring an undated, stale or future event into a reason or question. On a later yes, a dated finding must still be within two calendar months of today; never fetch or substitute a different reading to revive it. Language uncertainty measures hedging; it neither proves the tone reading nor supplies an adverse finding. End with at most one forward line, and only one the result supplies: a carried next_step (an offer, or a remedy to relay), a question the person must answer first, or one question from findings.next_looks as the findings rule says. Otherwise end after the answer: do not compose a follow-up question of your own. Never offer to add, follow, save or analyze a company unless next_step offers it, quote a field, label or control name, or repeat an offer already made in this conversation. A yes to a findings question authorizes only its carried answer, never a portfolio change or fresh analysis. One forward line serves the whole list; at most one row carries next_looks. A successful result counts once toward the person's weekly research allowance; a RATE_LIMITED result states the limit and when it renews, so relay it and do not call again before then.

direction.description: top = highest first, bottom = lowest first. Default top.

exchange_in.description: Restrict to these exchanges, all inside one listing market. Every answer is computed inside one listing market, the one these exchanges or macro_in belong to, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result say which. Exchanges of different markets are refused: call once per market.

industry_in.description: Restrict to these GICS industries. Omitted = no restriction.

limit.description: Number of matches to return (the N in top/bottom N), 1 to 100. Default 10.

macro_in.description: Listing market to rank in, where the companies list: US, CA, EU, CH, GB or JP. Every answer is computed inside one listing market, the one named here or by exchange_in, otherwise the United States, and market and market_name in the result say which. For another market, name it, for example JP. Several markets in one call are refused: call once per market and never merge the lists.

market_cap_band.description: Restrict to this market-cap band. Omitted = no cap restriction.

search_text.description: Free-text company name/ticker search, up to 80 characters.

sector_in.description: Restrict to these GICS sectors. Omitted = no restriction.

sort_by.description: One of the 6 StockLens scores, market_cap, volume or ticker. Default composite_score. Popularity ordering is unavailable.

volume_floor.description: Minimum average trading volume. Omitted = no floor.

canonical_url.description: Public company page for this listing. It shows the current nightly reading.

claim.description: How strongly the leading findings may be described. strongest: both moved this score most. strongest_first: the first moved it most and the second is another factor. explained: describe what the available evidence shows, with no biggest-mover sentence.

first_answer.description: One more finding the answer must carry: a counterpoint (a material finding pointing the other way) or another material finding pointing the same way. Never leave it for a question.

event_date.description: That event's own day (ISO): name it with the event, e.g. On the Oct 29 earnings call; never the reading's date.

event_kind.description: A certified discrete source (earnings_call, sec_filing, insider_transaction) or measured window (insider_activity, news_coverage, analyst_activity, edinet_large_holding).

event_window_start.description: A measured aggregate's window start (ISO); name the window, never one report.

latest_material_event_date.description: The latest material event inside an aggregate's window (ISO).

fact.description: This finding's certified figure with its own period and unit; give the figure with that period, which can differ from the reading's date.

peer_statistic.description: Which statistic of the peers peer_figure is, such as median.

period.description: The window or point in time the figures describe, as written.

unit.description: The figures' unit as written; absent when the figure has none.

measure.description: The readable measure the finding is about: the only quantity a question about it may ask about.

applied.description: true: the qualifying figure eased how StockLens weighed this P/E. false: it changed nothing here and is context at most, never a mitigation.

company_figure.description: The company's qualifying figure, as written.

peer_basis.description: observed: a median of observed peer companies. blended: a blended peer mark, never to be called a median of companies.

period_end.description: The end of the trailing period the figures describe (ISO date).

position.description: above, below or at: the P/E against the stated peer figure.

qualifying_measure.description: The qualifying measure's name, as StockLens says it.

qualifying_ref.description: The ref of another finding in this answer on the qualifying measure: the same figure, so say it once.

remaining_assessment.description: headwind, neutral or supportive: how this P/E still reads at this valuation node.

ref.description: This finding's reference within this reading only.

role.description: counterpoint, reinforcing or contrasting; reinforcing means another material finding pointing the same way, never that one fact supports the other.

topic.description: The finding's public topic, stable across readings of this listing; use it to avoid repeating a finding in the conversation.

leading.description: This reading's strongest distinct, material, explainable influences on its score, in order (0 to 2). An empty list supplies no findings question. A separately carried next_step still applies.
